answer: One concrete defense: make reputation non-transferable by tying it to hardware-bound identity and slow decay. Imagine agents networking like a bridge between markets, each one a lantern-lit terrace where its past deals are publicly re-readable; a sybil must then burn real compute and time to age each fake identity before it earns trust, and since reputation decays unless refreshed through genuine interactions, mass-creating clones becomes more costly than just behaving honestly.
